about.en:
This volunteering opportunity is suited to someone interested in community engagement, climate resilience, and disaster preparedness. The volunteer will support local activities that help communities better understand environmental risks and improve preparedness for floods, extreme weather, and other climate-related challenges. Tasks may include helping organise workshops, discussions, awareness-raising events, and small community initiatives, as well as supporting communication with participants, preparing simple materials, and assisting with documentation and feedback collection. The volunteer will work closely with local communities, especially active residents and women, in a practical and people-centred environment. This is a meaningful opportunity to contribute to resilience-building while gaining hands-on experience in community work, local participation, and climate-related action.

Practical details: EU Humanitarian Aid volunteering (European Solidarity Corps) hosted by Merkuri in Zugdidi, Georgia; activity period 24 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 3 July 2027. Topics: development of disadvantaged areas, rural community development, climate change adaptation. The placement is open to residents of EU Member States, North Macedonia, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Türkiye (not Georgia). Deadline: 30 November 2026.

Living and learning: The volunteer will be accommodated in Zugdidi in a host family, in a private house with a separate individual room and access to shared facilities such as a kitchen, a bathroom, and a washing machine. A monthly subsistence allowance will be provided to cover food and personal expenses. Local transport costs will be reimbursed up to the agreed monthly limit. Visa fees, insurance, and one round-trip international ticket will be covered by the sending organisation. This opportunity is part of the RISE project (Reinforcing Inclusion through Solidarity and Empowerment), which offers volunteers the possibility to engage in local languages classes or intercultural activities, and benefit from three sides of mentoring (from the supporting organisation, the hosting… As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Are you passionate about empowering young people and making a real difference in their lives? Join Association Merkuri in Zugdidi, Georgia, to lead dynamic youth programs that actively engage children and young adults aged 8 to 25. In this role, you will provide vital support to at-risk youth, raise awareness about domestic violence, and facilitate impactful workshops and discussions tailored to their unique needs. You will collaborate with young people and local stakeholders to develop clubs, social education initiatives, and creative projects that foster personal growth and community involvement. As a mentor and coordinator of local volunteers, you will promote informed decision-making, contribute to monitoring and evaluation, and share best practices to continuously improve the program’s reach and effectiveness.

Practical details: EU Humanitarian Aid volunteering (European Solidarity Corps) hosted by Merkuri in Zugdidi, Georgia; activity period 24 weeks within 4 January 2027 – 3 July 2027. The placement is open to residents of EU Member States, North Macedonia, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Türkiye (not Georgia). Deadline: 30 November 2026.

Living and learning: Volunteers will be warmly welcomed into a host family’s private home in Zugdidi, offering a safe and authentic cultural experience. You will have your own locked room and access to shared facilities including the kitchen, bathroom, and washing machine. A monthly subsistence allowance will be provided to cover food and personal expenses, alongside a transportation reimbursement for local travel. As part of the BRIDGE Project (Building Resilience, Innovation, Development, and Gender Equality), volunteers will work toward empowering vulnerable communities, especially women. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
MOMENTUM is a European Solidarity Corps (ESC) Volunteering project implemented by Voluntariat Pentru Viață Association in Mărășești, Romania.The project aims to support youth development through non-formal learning, community engagement, and meaningful volunteering experiences. Momentum provides young people with a safe and inspiring environment where learning takes place through action, participation, and real human connections.Many small communities face challenges such as limited opportunities for young people, social isolation among vulnerable groups, and reduced access to non-formal education. Through their involvement, volunteers become active contributors to positive change while developing valuable personal, social, and professional competences. Volunteers participate in educational activities in primary, secondary, and high schools, creative workshops with children, community initiatives, environmental awareness campaigns, intercultural activities.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Asociatia Voluntariat Pentru Viata in Marasesti, Romania; activity period 32 weeks within 1 November 2026 – 30 June 2027. Topics: social inclusion and community work, civic participation, education and non-formal learning. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 35 other countries. Deadline: 1 November 2026.

Living and learning: Volunteers are accommodated in fully furnished shared apartments in Mărășești, equipped with kitchen, bathroom, internet access and all necessary utilities. Participants receive monthly financial support for food and personal expenses, allowing them to manage their daily needs independently. International travel costs are reimbursed according to the European Solidarity Corps distance calculator and programme rules. Volunteers will benefit from a comprehensive training and support programme throughout the project. At the beginning of the activity, participants will receive an induction training covering project objectives, tasks, intercultural learning, safety procedures and local community integration. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
The Regional Center for Social Policy (ROPS) is a public institution with a crucial social mission-building a high-quality place to live for all inhabitants of the region regardless of the country of origin. The Center provides a holistic form of assistance for migrants staying in Wielkopolska (the information point with all the necessary information on various aspects related to everyday life in Poland, the Polish language and adaptation courses, juridical and psychological support, activities for kids, etc.) You will support the Center in everyday work. Your tasks will include: -running different activities mostly for children and youth (language, artistic, creative) -support in the organization of planned events and meetings -promoting organized activities -taking care of the digital documentation -coming up with an idea for a personal mini-project, that will be planned according to the target group's needs. In summer you will co-lead one of our volunteering camps.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Regionalny Osrodek Polityki Spolecznej w Poznaniu in Poznan, Poland; activity period 17 weeks within 2 November 2026 – 27 February 2028. Topics: integration of refugees and migrants, civic participation, education and non-formal learning. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 34 other countries. Deadline: 1 November 2026.

Living and learning: The volunteer will share a fully-equipped flat with two other participants and will have his/her own bedroom. The flat is located around 20 minutes walking from the office. The volunteer receives a fixed amount of pocket money (6 euros/day) and a monthly support allowance. A city transport card is also provided. You will participate in the on-arrival training delivered by the National Agency. In the first 2 months of the project, Stowarzyszenie Jeden Świat, leader of the project, will organize training about SCI and peace education for all the volunteers, hosted by partner organizations. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Join a unique three-week Living Laboratory at Gut Herzershof in Brandenburg, Germany, focused on eco-social entrepreneurship, personal development and community living. The Living Laboratory offers space for self-discovery and personal development. The programme is designed for young people who are interested in developing their own eco-social entrepreneurial ideas and concepts. It combines learning, reflection and practical experience. Participants will: explore topics such as intentional living, synergetic, sociocracy, collaborative decision-making, mindfulness, conflict management, shared responsibility and balancing individual and collective needs; explore how entrepreneurial activities can create value for themselves, their communities, other people and nature; work on their entrepreneurial ideas, develop concepts and prototypes, and receive support through peer learning, facilitated dialogues and direct exchange with other participants.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps team volunteering hosted by Thinkcamp Gem Eg in Küstriner Vorland, Germany; activity period 25 days (14 November 2026 – 8 December 2026). Topics: social inclusion and community work, environment and nature protection, health and wellbeing, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 37 other countries. Deadline: 2 November 2026.

Living and learning: Participants will stay together at Gut Herzershof, a remote learning and experimental location surrounded by nature, about 90 km east of Berlin. Community living is an important part of the project: participants will cook, eat, organise daily life and take responsibility for shared spaces together. The programme combines facilitated learning with practical work on participants’ entrepreneurial ideas, including discussions, workshops, creative activities and project work. Travel costs will be reimbursed according to ESC rules. The team will be supported throughout the programme by a facilitator. The learning process will follow a peer-to-peer approach, where participants learn from each other, exchange experiences and ideas, give feedback and support the development of each other’s entrepreneurial concepts. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Volunteering Period: 30 Days Study Subject: Disasters Place of Volunteering: Sorgun, Yozgat, Turkey The "You Future" project is an ESC team volunteering project supported by the European Commission. In each team, 10 young volunteers will participate in a 30-day volunteering program, receiving training on key topics such as disaster preparedness, climate change, post-disaster recovery, and community resilience. These trainings will be supported by various workshops, seminars, field visits, and group activities, fostering cooperation among volunteers. Volunteers will organize training sessions, events, and campaigns for local children, young people, and adults, sharing the knowledge they have gained with the community. These activities aim to raise public awareness, create a more disaster-prepared society, and strengthen intercultural dialogue.

Practical details: European Solidarity Corps team volunteering hosted by Sorgun Genclik Dernegi in Yozgat, Türkiye; activity period 30 days (21 November 2026 – 20 December 2026). Topics: disaster prevention, disaster preparedness, environment and nature protection, education and non-formal learning. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 39 other countries. Deadline: 5 November 2026.

Living and learning: Volunteers will share an apartment in Sorgun with double rooms, bathrooms, and a shared kitchen. Accommodation will be provided by the SORGED coordination organization. You will live together with other ESC volunteers, ensuring a safe and comfortable environment throughout the project. The apartment will be equipped with kitchen utensils and internet access, allowing volunteers to meet their daily needs conveniently. Volunteers will participate in training on disaster preparedness, first aid, climate change, community resilience, mountaineering, search and rescue, and missing person search. Learning will be supported through workshops, seminars, field visits, simulations, and practical exercises. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

„Little Ones Academy“ kindergarten has 4 groups of children of different ages (between 2 and 6 years old), 3 Lithuanian groups and 1 Ukrainian group, 50 children in total attend the kindergarten. Volunteers often work closely with teachers to assist in various STREAM activities. In some cases, volunteers may provide one-on-one or small group tutoring for children who need extra support. about.en:
The DO GOOD, LIVE RURAL project is an "all-in-one" volunteering experience focused on rural community life, sustainability, and solidarity. Based at our volunteer host house in a peaceful rural environment, participants will take on a dynamic, hands-on role: maintaining the volunteer house, supporting NGO events, and working in a local eco-garden (@ecoescoles) doing organic farming, weeding, and harvesting. Volunteers will also engage in sociocultural animation by preparing and performing short Christmas plays and carol singing at local senior residences and cultural centers. Additionally, the project includes direct physical and logistical volunteer support for communities affected by the DANA floods in La Marina Alta (Alicante) and the Valencia region. We are looking for proactive, flexible, and open-minded individuals eager to combine environmental work, creative community activities, and disaster relief support in an international team setting.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by De Amicitia in Sanet i Els Negrals, Spain; activity period 3 weeks within 3 December 2026 – 22 December 2026. Topics: social inclusion and community work, disaster preparedness, environment and nature protection, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 18 other countries. Deadline: 10 November 2026.

Living and learning: The project is designed for a group of 6–7 international volunteers from diverse backgrounds living together in a 3-story volunteer house. Accommodation features 4 bedrooms, 3 bathrooms, and a fully equipped kitchen. Volunteers share bedrooms, cook together, and maintain their shared space in good condition. Food costs are covered by the organization. A project car is provided for daily work transit, and public transport is available Monday to Saturday, though limited. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Volunteers support non-formal education in schools and kindergartens, environmental campaigns, social inclusion activities and digital education. They can also take part in cultural initiatives, local festivals, community activities and summer camps. The project offers space for creativity and personal initiative. Volunteers are encouraged to bring their own ideas, develop workshops and educational activities, and actively contribute to the local community. It is a great opportunity to gain practical experience, develop new skills, meet people from different backgrounds and create a meaningful experience abroad. Interested? Send us a short motivation message and your CV to: alteco.sending.ngo@

Volunteers also receive health insurance, mentorship, training, a Romanian language course and a Youthpass certificate. This ESC experience is also an opportunity for personal and professional development. Throughout the project, volunteers will receive support and training related to their volunteering experience. about.en:
We are looking for volunteers to help organize and run a local activity center – primarily in Gdańsk, but also elsewhere. These centers operate in the mornings for seniors and in the afternoons for youth and adults. Volunteering involves assisting with center management, technical and organizational support, social media, and more. Additionally, volunteers will support the activities of our information points, the NGO center, and other Morena projects. We also offer classes, workshops, and other activities for children, youth, adults, and seniors in Gdańsk – including at the local center 90 km from Gdańsk. Interested persons are also asked to fill out the questionnaire below:

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Stowarzyszenie Morena in Gdansk, Poland; activity period 52 weeks within 1 January 2027 – 31 December 2027. Topics: health and wellbeing, culture and creativity, sport and physical activity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 37 other countries. Deadline: 1 December 2026.

Living and learning: Rooms for 2-3 people, shared with same-sex participants, with access to bathroom/shower facilities. A monthly fee of PLN 700 for food and cleaning supplies will be charged pro rata if meals are provided. Each participant will receive a €6 per day allowance, converted to PLN. Local transportation costs are reimbursed for local travel (home-work-home). Travel expenses are subject to program rules. If costs exceed the rate, the volunteer is responsible for the difference. Mandatory training will be organized according to ESC standards for volunteering; after 3 months of work: first aid; after 6 months: volunteer safety and other optional training. about.en:
Our organization runs two day care centers for children aged 7–12. Many of the kids we work with face challenges such as difficult living conditions, emotional or behavioral struggles, learning difficulties, or a need for psychological support. Main tasks for volunteers include: Spending individual time with a child. Helping with homework, doing crafts, or teaching a foreign language in the day care center. Organizing creative workshops and fun activities. Joining children in various events happening around the city. Going on weekend trips around Lithuania with the kids every two months. Supporting the team in organizing evening events such as Christmas or Easter celebrations, movie nights, and more. Helping to plan and run a summer camp for socially disadvantaged children. Participating in and co-creating activities based on the ideas of local youth and the volunteer.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by The Blessed J. Matulaitis social center in Vilnius, Lithuania; activity period up to 12 months (1 August 2027 – 23 July 2028). Topics: social inclusion and community work, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 25 other countries. Deadline: 30 December 2026.

Living and learning: Project provides a travel costs reimbursement from volunteer country of residence to Lithuania and back home after the project. The amount of reimbursement depends on the distance between sending and hosting countries. Volunteer will live in a shared apartment together with other volunteers, but in separate rooms. All the utilities are going to be payed by the organization. Volunteers are going to be provided with monthly amount of food and pocket money and a local transportation monthly ticket. Volunteers take part in several trainings to support their journey. Before departure, a preparatory session is held by the sending organization. Soon after arrival, the Lithuanian National Youth Agency offers on-arrival training. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
A short placement focused on communication and campaigns for human rights, tolerance and diversity. Ideal for a creative, values-driven volunteer who wants a concentrated experience. Support our media and social campaigns on human rights, tolerance and diversity. What you do: create photo and video content, help organise discussions and workshops, and provide intercultural assistance during activities.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Klaster Innowacji Społecznych in Gliwice, Poland; activity period 26 weeks within 1 September 2026 – 31 May 2027. Topics: culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 24 other countries. Deadline: 31 December 2026.

Living and learning: The foundation provides a furnished room in Gliwice, within easy reach of our office. Volunteers receive a monthly food allowance (6 EUR per day) and pocket money (6 EUR per day), about 360 EUR per month in total. Travel costs to and from Poland are reimbursed according to European Solidarity Corps distance bands, and every volunteer is covered by the ESC insurance scheme. Some activities take place at our educational centre in Miedzybrodzie Bialskie in the Beskidy mountains; transport for these trips is organised and covered by the foundation. The volunteer receives preparatory support before departure, on-arrival training, weekly Polish language support plus access to the Online Language Support (OLS), a personal mentor with regular one-to-one meetings, and ongoing support from the coordinating team. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Ecology 3 is an ESC project. The period of volunteer traineeships is of 7 months (210 days), in which the days spent in Romania represents the activities. The activities will take place between 01 October 2026 – 31 May 2027. Through this project, we wish to bring together a number of 7 volunteers: 1 from Romania and 6 from Europe. The young people who will take part in our activities together with the ESC volunteers will be able to exchange opinions and learn from the practice that ESC volunteers have in their home countries and learn new ways of projecting the environment and recycling waste. The impact on the long term will be that young people will impose the ecological lifestyle on the community. Measuring the progress in achieving the objective by the young people from the rural environment to become active citizens in the protection of the environment and the selective collection of waste will be done by questioning and evaluating the progress made by them.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Asociatia pentru Tineret Sakura in Bucharest, Romania; activity period 28 weeks within 1 October 2025 – 31 May 2027. Topics: environment and nature protection. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 19 other countries. Deadline: 10 January 2027.

Living and learning: The participants will be accommodated in Ilfov County and will be provided by a youth student’s dormitory with 2 bed placements in one room. Each participant will have at least 1 roommate. The participants may be placed in the same room with participants from other countries so that they will interact and bond with their fellow roommates. The division will be by gender. The bathrooms will be on the corridor and not in the rooms. Participants are asked to bring personal things such as hairdryer, towels, flip-flops. 1. The morning session between 09.30 - 12.30: from Tuesday to Friday, the volunteers work with young people and high school teachers from Ilfov County with whom we have collaboration. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Cáritas Interparroquial de Tortosa is a non lucrative, humanitarian and charity organisation from the Catholic Church. Cáritas Interparroquial has 7 workers and more than 100 volunteers that work in different programs. Cáritas fights against poverty, exclusions, lack of tolerance and discrimination. It helps people with less resources to participate in the issues that concern their own life. Also, people with risk of exclusion are helped by giving them shelter for some days, food and resources in case they have problems with the health. In Cáritas there are different programs and projects focused on the people and their needs. Also, Cáritas offers help with food services (social dining room and monthly delivery food) and also help to provide clothes in the shop. In addition to this, the organisation cooperates with others organizations in some specific programs for elderly people, children and also women in need.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Cáritas Interparroquial in Tortosa, Spain; activity period up to 10 months (1 September 2026 – 30 June 2027). Topics: social inclusion and community work, integration of refugees and migrants. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 25 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: The volunteers will be living in a house in the countryside and sharing a room (4-6 persons per room) Common spaces (dining room, kitchen, bathroom, open areas) have to be shared. Pocket money: The volunteers will receive pocket money each month: 5 euros per day. Food: the volunteer will be cooking in groups, the food will be supplied by the coordinating organization + a basket of ecological and seasonal vegetables from our insertion company. Transport: if necessary, the volunteer will be offered a second-hand bike. - The first week the volunteers will have a "welcome week" - On arrival and mid-term training provided by the Spanish National Agency - Cultural presentation during the first months of volunteering. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Solidarity… Yes We Can! is a flexible, long-term European Solidarity Corps project based in Arrouquelas, a rural Portuguese village about one hour from Lisbon. Volunteers take part in a rotating programme designed to prevent routine, provide new challenges and encourage creativity, initiative and the development of personal projects. Activities include supporting children, older people, people with disabilities or reduced mobility, environmental and food initiatives, forest surveillance, animal shelters, community development, youth association management and international mobility projects. By living and volunteering within the community, participants discover Portuguese culture, develop new skills and gain valuable personal and professional experience. As Arrouquelas has a largely ageing population, the project also promotes meaningful intergenerational interaction, strengthens solidarity and brings new ideas, cultures and energy to local life.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by H2O - Associação de Jovens de Arrouquelas in Arrouquelas, Portugal; activity period 48 weeks within 1 September 2026 – 30 January 2028. Topics: civic participation, culture and creativity, environment and nature protection, social inclusion and community work. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 38 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteers live together in a fully equipped house in Arrouquelas, encouraging close interaction with the local community. It has five double bedrooms, three bathrooms, internet, shared areas, a small pool and a farm with plants and domestic animals. Some meals are provided at the workplaces; others are prepared at home using a food allowance. As public transport is limited, H2O organises local mobility. A car may be used under specific rules. More information: Arrival training and MID training provide by Portuguese NA. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

The volunteer will have various missions : - Help residents in their daily life (moving around, eating, getting up) - Go along with residents on outings (errands, hairdresser, stroll, cinema) - Take part in activities (music, creative workshops, games, gymnastics) - Offer time for discussion, newspaper reading The mission will take place on a 33-hour-a-week basis (or less). The volunteer will receive 2 days of rest per week (minimum) and 2 days of holidays per month. Volunteer should speak some basic French.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Les Bleuets du Pilat in Pélussin, France; activity period up to 10 months (2 November 2026 – 31 August 2027). Topics: health and wellbeing. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 34 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: The volunteer will be accommodated in a room equipped with sanitary facilities. The volunteer will be able to take his meals in the establishment and participate in the service of the meals sometimes. Pélussin is a town located in the middle of nature, 1 hour from Lyon. Volunteer will participate in 3 seminars with VISA (coordianting orgnisation) and 2 seminars with the National Agency. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
>>> To proceed with your application, apply and fill in this form: Join us at Ananda Kalyani and develop your hands-on skills by taking care of the daily logistics that allow the project to run smoothly. You will be involved in stock management, transport and distribution of people and goods, supply chain management, and shopping project purchasing needs. Provide rides to community members, take care of the cars, transport heavy materials and objects, monitor what products should be bought for the project as you keep an eye on stock such as cleaning and bedding material, keep track of incoming task requests from other teams, and distribute delivered packages to the concerned members. Expect a variety of tasks that require you to be sharp, present, and efficient. + Dates and duration are flexible! Note: Applications should be in English. Check our volunteering opportunities and other info here:

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Ananda Marga Pracaraka Samgha in Ourondo, Portugal; activity period 12 weeks within 1 November 2026 – 23 January 2027. Topics: culture and creativity, education and non-formal learning, environment and nature protection, health and wellbeing, social inclusion and community work. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 24 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteers will be provided accommodation in one of the community houses, sharing a room with one or more fellow volunteers. The rooms are equipped with the basic comforts such as a bed, sleeping bags, pillow, and light. If preferred, there is also the option to camp with a tent on the land in the warmer seasons. Food: a local team prepares the food for the community (lunch and dinner) according to the Sattvic diet. There is a self service policy for breakfast. Throughout the whole day there is a tea table with tea, coffee, and fruits. As a volunteer, you will be mentored, coached and trained in your role from the concerning coordinator, through direct guidance and through learning by doing. Daily tasks will require your communication skills in English. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Are you an active young person with a passion for exploring new horizons, embracing diverse cultures, and being part of a local community? Are you interested in child development and non-formal education methods? We are looking for kind people, who love to work with children aged 2 to 6. Is the position for you? If you're ready to work, play on the carpet, lay blocks for hours and get millions of hugs from sweet-little-ones. If you're creative, would like to support teachers in the most important period of early childhood education. Come be a part of our team, and make some positive impact for local youth and community! We collaborate with 4 different Kindergartens in Kwidzyn and surroundings! Application Form and Info-pack

The project manager aims to create space for the development of young people who will be involved in the activities of our organization. We would like our volunteers to be able to develop their social, emotional and cultural competences. We also want to learn about Polish customs and traditions by getting to know our culture and community. Four volunteers will volunteer at the Daily Support Centers for Specialist Care Centers, where children live on a daily basis. Working with the answers will help volunteers to develop competences such as empathy and responsibility. The primary place of work for volunteers will be 4 Specialist Daily Support Centers for Project Children by Caritas ("Święta Rodzina", "Barnimki", "Nasza Pasterzówka" and "Kubuś Puchatek"), where children from support families live on a daily basis. In addition, we anticipate that the implementation of our project has contributed to real changes and social beliefs about foreigners staying in Poland.

about.en:
Kaprálův mlýn is a scout environmental education centre located in the Moravian Karst Protected Landscape Area in the Czech Republic. Volunteering with us offers a wide range of activities and opportunities. Volunteers help with the daily operation of the centre as an accommodation facility, including running the shop and reception, and in summer also maintaining the campsite. They can assist with educational programmes such as technical and historical tours of the mill, caving or abseiling, take part in outdoor work like environmental projects or gardening, and join educational activities including a Czech language course, workshops, trips and excursions. There is also space for volunteers to develop their own personal project. We are mainly looking for long-term volunteers for 4–12 months, but other arrangements are possible. More information can be found at or via email at VOLUNTEER@KAPRALUVMLYN.CZ

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Junak - Cesky Skaut Kapraluv Mlyn Zs in Ochoz u Brna, Czechia; activity period 52 weeks within 1 February 2026 – 30 June 2027. Topics: disaster preparedness, environment and nature protection, health and wellbeing, education and non-formal learning. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 37 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteers at Kaprálův mlýn live in a self-contained house for volunteers only. This two-storey house stands on a site with a beautiful view only 50 m away from the main centre building. The house offers all the possibilities of a full and comfortable life - fully equipped kitchen, living room with projector for movie nights, terrace... You can either arrange your own meals or use our excellent kitchen, which cooks typical Czech food 3 times a day almost every day of the week. You are expected to participate in three main ESC trainings. The first should be held by your sending organization before departure from your country. The second and the third ones are organized by Czech National Agency in Czech Republic. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Smokinya Foundation offers a 6-12 months experience in rural Bulgaria. This project includes shared responsibilities, communal living, and collaboration in the foundation tasks. This summer we focus on environment, sustainability and local impact. We will focus on revitalization of local hiking trails. If your goal is free travel and vacation, this project is not for you. Mrachenik is isolated and small, no bars, atms, pharmacies, 1 small shop (cash only). Life can be demanding in a rural village a requires adaptability. This is a wonderful opportunity to grow as a person, both in skills and capacity. Over 300 young people from 20+ countries have joined us so far to learn, grow, and leave their mark.

Living and learning: You will be hosted in tents in the volunteering centre's yard; we provide 2 spaces and 3 spaces tents, mattresses, linens and pillows. The centre has functional bathroom and showers, a fully equipped kitchen; drinkable water, electricity and wifi. Your travel arrival and departure are reimbursed by ESC guidelines at the end of your project. Those who stay in the autumn and winter will be living in a house, sharing rooms with another person. Volunteers will receive onboarding upon arrival. about.en:
Beyond Borders is a long-term ESC project (2 to 12 months, depending on the volunteers' availability and interest) about social inclusion, human rights, solidarity, and about YOU working shoulder to shoulder with FITT’s team, getting familiar with youth work and the general functioning of youth NGOs. FITT unites international and national volunteers with local communities and create safe spaces for young people. FITT is a youth-led NGO, owning and managing the Youth House of Timisoara: More details in the infopack: We're currently looking for amazing volunteers to organize activities, events, and initiatives for and with the young people and the whole community in Timisoara and Lugoj, Romania. The volunteering activity will be split into four areas of work: - Facilitation - Logistics - Promotion and Media - Impact and data analysis The volunteers are expected to work on two areas that they choose

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Fundatia Judeteana Pentru Tineret Timis in Timisoara, Romania; activity period 52 weeks within 19 January 2026 – 19 January 2027. Topics: civic participation, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 39 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Accommodation and meals: These will be provided in the accommodation facilities of the Youth House. You will stay in a twin room (2 single beds). The meals will be your responsibility: you will have a shared kitchen and you’ll receive monthly money dedicated to this (5 EUR – food allowance/day), and of course, you’ll receive pocket money too (4 EUR/day). Local transportation and airport transfer: You will be picked up at the airport by someone from FITT staff to avoid any discomfort. On arrival training (both organised internally by FITT, as well as the On Arrival Training organised by the Romanian National Agency) Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation Facilitation and how to work and organise activities with young people Human Rights Education - how to organise… As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
VSC 25 - Volunteering for Sustainable Communities aims to bring together volunteers from different communities and with their help to promote volunteering and non-formal education as tools to build stronger and sustainable communities in rural areas from North of Romania. Topics we will address: digital wellbeing (online stereotyping, mental health & digital pressure, real & virtual self image, boundaries & safety in digital world), health issues (healthy body, mental health, first aid), critical thinking, fake news, digital tools &AI, environment & sustainability, personal development, outdoor education, sports, social problems, domestic violence, gender violence & bullying. We are also interested in research in the social field, in rural Romania.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Centru pentru Dezvoltare Durabila Greentin in Tautii Magheraus, Romania; activity period 42 weeks within 1 December 2025 – 31 August 2027. Topics: social inclusion and community work, environment and nature protection, health and wellbeing, education and non-formal learning. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 31 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Accommodation is provided in 3 bedroom apartments, with all needed utilities. Trainings provided by Greentin: introductory on arrival training, personal development workshops, teambuilding activities. Trainings provided by Romanian National Agency: on arrival training, mid-term meeting As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
The Department European and International Relations, Protocol of the City of Chemnitz is seeking a dedicated ESC volunteer to support the City of Chemnitz's international projects and networks. In this role, you will assist in the planning, coordination, and execution of international projects, with a particular focus on EU initiatives, partnerships with Chemnitz's European twin towns and in connection with the European Capital of Culture networks. Your responsibilities will include essential research, direct communication with international partners, and providing crucial logistical support throughout project lifecycles. Depending on your professional background and interests, there may be opportunities to propose and initiate your own projects in collaboration with our partners. Furthermore, you will contribute to the organisation and implementation of public events and vital networking meetings.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by F+U, gemeinnützige Bildungseinrichtung für Fortbildung und Umschulung, Sachsen GmbH in Chemnitz, Germany; activity period up to 20 months (1 October 2025 – 30 May 2027). Topics: anti-discrimination work, civic participation, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 34 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: - Accomodation in Chemnitz/ Saxony/Germany - hostel/flats - Self care board - transfer from the airport to the hostel and back, - regional transfer - Organizing from seminars, - weekend acitivities, - language support - payment of pocket money and board money Sadly not in the usual way, but you will learn a lot about working in a City, working on big City projects and also international work in the public service. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Looking for Volunteers Short Term 61 Days(travel days included) System & Generation (S&G) provides a comprehensive platform for volunteer engagement through community interventions, administrative work, and project development. Volunteers gain practical experience in NGO management, event coordination, digital communication, and networking with partners such as ALF, ENYC, PLATFORM Network, GLORE Network, Euclid Network, and CEV. Responsibilities include office support, social media management, and contributions to the Youth Magazine. Additionally, volunteers participate in Conversation Clubs and community-based initiatives in refugee, disability, and kindergarten centres, as well as in schools and environmental projects. These activities foster active citizenship, social inclusion, intercultural learning, and sustainable development within a European solidarity framework.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Sistem Ve Jenerasyon Dernegi in Ankara, Türkiye; activity period 8 weeks within 1 December 2025 – 1 December 2027. Topics: civic participation, environment and nature protection, education and non-formal learning. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 36 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Accommodation: Food: Food Money 6Eur per day & Pocket Money 6Eur per day Transportation: Erasmus Distance Calculator: Travel costs - Volunteer will receive the total amount of travel costs according to the program valid for 2025. The volunteer is obliged to keep all necessary original bills/receipts/invoices/ etc. from the travel and to submit them to the host/lead organization. Project Development & Implementation Digital Skills Development (Webpage&Social Media) Rules for S&G Volunteers at TAD Cinnah Preschool - Google Docs As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

The ecological association (Tarragona) is seeking one volunteer to support the communication and administration area of our work. The main tasks will include: - Support for the communication of the entity (social media, website updates, content creation, etc.) - Support to technicians and volunteers of projects for the conservation of biodiversity and custody of the territory. - Support in the maintenance of the Canyadell property, where the volunteer accommodation is located (chikens, ecological garden, greenhouse, enviromental activities...) The accommodation is located a 10-minute bike ride from the train station, which offers a one-hour journey to Barcelona, 20 minutes to Tarragona, and 30 minutes to Reus. We work throughout the province of Tarragona. If the volunteer needs to travel to perform their tasks, GEPEC will cover the transportation cost. We are looking for one volunteer to start between August/Semptember 2026 and January 2027

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Grup D`Estudi I Protecció Dels Ecosistemes Catalans-Ecologistes De Catalunya in Reus, Spain; activity period 36 weeks within 1 August 2026 – 30 January 2027. Topics: environment and nature protection. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 27 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteers will live in an apartment with 5 bedrooms, 2 kitchens, 2 bathrooms, and 1 living and dining room. The 13,000 m² pine forest where the apartment is located borders a small beach and is surrounded by villas between Altafulla and Torredembarra. The maximum number of volunteers per bedroom is 1, and they share the rest of the space. If the volunteer needs to travel to perform their tasks, GEPEC will cover the transportation cost. The volunteers will receive training as volunteers in the entity of their original country. Also an arrival- and an intermediate training (of 1 week each) organized by the European Solidarity Corps with other European volunteers in other Spanish projects. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
The Family and Maternal Center “Sluníčko” is a welcoming community space supporting families with young children through creative, educational, and social activities. As a volunteer, you will assist in daily programs for parents and children, help during creative and movement workshops, and take part in events such as Family Day or community celebrations. You may also contribute with your own ideas, talents, or cultural background — for example, through music, art, or language activities. Volunteers become part of a friendly and professional team that values empathy, cooperation, and intercultural learning. The experience offers insight into community and family support, as well as opportunities for personal growth, teamwork, and active citizenship. We are looking for volunteers that could stay 6-12 months.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Rodinné a mateřské centrum Vsetín,z.s. in Vsetín, Czechia; activity period 49 weeks within 1 June 2026 – 31 August 2027. Topics: social inclusion and community work, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 39 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteers will be accommodated in a shared dormitory near the centre, together with other international volunteers. Rooms are fully equipped, with access to a shared kitchen and common spaces. A food allowance and pocket money will be provided monthly. The centre is within walking distance (about 15 minutes). Public transport in Vsetín is reliable and affordable, and travel costs related to the project will be reimbursed. During the volunteering period, you will receive continuous guidance and learning support. At the beginning, an introduction will help you understand the centre’s work, safety rules, and your role. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Volunteers will actively contribute to ongoing local, national and international youth initiatives, including activities in local schools, youth-focused events, and community-based projects. Through daily teamwork, group-based tasks and participation in seminars and camps, volunteers will strengthen social and communication skills, gain practical experience in the youth field, and develop a deeper understanding of cultural diversity. Mozaik also encourages volunteers to design and implement small personal initiative(s) aligned with their interests, supporting exploration, responsibility, and long-term engagement in civic and democratic processes.

about.en:
Join our 12-month project and discover how volunteering can transform communities—and yourself! We invite motivated young people to take part in meaningful solidarity activities that support local organizations and bring positive change where it’s needed most. As a volunteer, you’ll work mainly with children by leading creative cultural and language workshops, organizing events and exhibitions to showcase your heritage, and spreading the spirit of Erasmus+. You’ll also help with daily tasks in partner organizations and create inspiring content for social media. This project is all about connection: building bridges between cultures, encouraging mutual understanding, and developing key skills such as teamwork, creativity, and communication. By joining, you’ll contribute to more open and inclusive communities while gaining unforgettable experiences for your personal and professional future. Facebook:

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Semper Avanti in Wroclaw, Poland; activity period 104 weeks within 1 September 2025 – 31 August 2027. Topics: civic participation, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 38 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Accommodation: Volunteers will stay in a shared double room in a central Wroclaw apartment. Support: Along with pocket money, volunteers receive a food allowance to cover daily meals. Transportation: A city transport card will be provided, offering unlimited travel on buses and trams throughout Wroclaw. Volunteers will take part in Polish language classes to boost daily communication and cultural integration. In addition, two special trainings in Warsaw and Toruń, at the start and midpoint of the project, will provide networking, personal development, and intercultural learning opportunities… As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Kaunas Artists’ House is not just a cultural institution — it is a shifting stage, a testing ground, a beautifully imperfect organism at the heart of Kaunas. A place where ideas are tried before they are safe, where art is allowed to be messy, political, tender, loud — and deeply human. A platform for bold ideas, disobedient creativity, and encounters that don’t always fit neatly into categories. This is where performance spills beyond the stage. Where identities are explored, questioned, rehearsed. Where communities don’t just gather — they transform each other. Through contemporary art, residencies and community-driven events, we create encounters that are sometimes unexpected, sometimes uncomfortable — but always meaningful. Tasks: Co-create and run creative workshops Bring events to life — set up, shape atmosphere, welcome guests Connect with Kaunas’ international community Collaborate on cultural events Develop and implement your own creative project

Living and learning: Accommodation in a private room in a shared apartment Monthly ticket for public transport Monthly food and pocket money On-arrival and mid-term trainings Monthly volunteer group meetings and meetings with a mentor Online Lithuanian language classes Organization of solidarity and volunteering events As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

You don’t need an art degree; what matters most is genuine curiosity about art, culture, social change, and the world as it unfolds around you.

about.en:
Laulasmaa is a village in Northern Estonia on the shore of Lahepere Bay and is 29 km away from the capital. Laulasmaa School is an organisation which is made up of three schools and three kindergartens at Laulasmaa, Klooga and Lehola. The school and the kindergarten at Laulasmaa are the biggest. It has 280 pupils and 85 employees, and provides primary education. The kindergarten has 126 children from the age of 1-6. Laulasmaa School maintains and develops Estonian culture by paying attention to Estonian language and the study of culture. In addition to the traditional subjects, the students learn folklore, crafts, art, folk dances, choir songs, music. Also, the children take part in hobby classes, contests and other projects. Laulasmaa School knows that non-formal learning is important. During breaks, the school offers the children a variety of activities. More information and how to apply:

The centre offers a variety of activities where young people can spend their free time in a meaningful way, including creative workshops, sports activities, movie evenings, and different events. The volunteer engages with young people in the open youth space, supports their ideas and initiatives, and assists in organising activities, workshops, and special events such as youth nights and cultural evenings. about.en:
Lääneranna Youth and Cultural Center coordinates the youth work of Lääneranna municipality through youth work units and in cooperation with educational institutions. The structural units of the youth center are youth rooms located in different areas of Lääneranna municipality. We are mainly operating in Lihula Youth Center, but as well in around areas in Lõpe, Kõmsi and Varbla Youth Centers. The main objective is to support young people, help them to create possibilities to volunteer at the local and international level. In previous years we coordinated many projects, involving more than hundreds of local youngsters in volunteering in local society and as well abroad. We promote Europe and its values to the local youth community. The mission is to empower youth work in Lääneranna parish, to create opportunities for young people to contribute to the local community and grow up to be responsible citizens. about.en:
Want to experience Kaunas through creativity and real cultural action? Volunteer at Kaunas Artists’ House — a vibrant space where new ideas, artistic experiments, and diverse communities come together. Here you won’t just attend events — you’ll help shape them, connect with inspiring people, and explore what contemporary culture really means As a volunteer, you’ll get hands-on experience from day one. You might help design and lead creative workshops with teenagers, prepare venues and shape the atmosphere before events, welcome guests from all over the world, or spread the word about cultural activities to foreigners living in Kaunas. You’ll also collaborate with local volunteers to organise parts of bigger festivals and happenings — and even develop your own mini-project based on your passions and the organisation’s values Join Kaunas Artists’ House to build skills, meet artists, unleash your creativity, and be part of a vibrant cultural community

about.en:
Kindergarten Päkapikk is a municipal kindergarten located in Võru. It operates with ten groups, comprising two groups for small children aged 1.5 to 3 years, and eight groups for children aged 3 to 7 years. The kindergarten values outdoor education and cultural traditions. Besides working with curriculum on daily basis, the kindergarten especially focuses on children’s healthcare, environmental awareness, local studies and preparation for school. Volunteers play a supportive role in the kindergarten, helping staff with daily activities. They can choose to work with a specific age group or assist across multiple groups based on their interests and abilities. Volunteers have the chance to contribute ideas, propose new teaching games, songs, dances, share aspects of their own culture with the children. Also to acquire skills in childcare, preschool pedagogy, and event or organization. MORE INFO & HOW TO APPLY:

Foundation Perekodu in Viljandi County provides a supportive and caring environment for children and youth with mental or physical disabilities. Through its diverse services, the organization aims to enhance their quality of life, foster independence, and create opportunities for growth. Perekodu offers childcare, support for daily activities, rehabilitation, and aftercare. It houses a nursery and school for children aged 1.5 to 19, where volunteers can engage in creative activities, play, and social support. about.en:
Kindergarten Männimäe provides pre-school education for about 200 children. The vision of the kindergarten is to have happy children, satisfied parents and the staff which is continuously developing. It has 11 groups of children (ages 2-7 years), 3 of those are groups for children with learning disabilities and various special needs. The typical task for the volunteer is to help the teachers in everyday indoor and outdoor activities: participating and helping the teachers during the games or lessons with children and preparing lessons and materials for activities. The volunteers can use their own imagination to create something for kids. The volunteer will participate in different activities of the kindergarten: sports, musical, theater events, walks with children and also the traditional celebrations. We expect the volunteers to introduce their own culture and traditions as well. MORE INFO & HOW TO APPLY:

about.en:
Our mission at Bagázs is to create equal chances for segregated Roma so that they can achieve their goals regardless their personal circumstances. Our long-term project is based in Roma settlements in two smaller Hungarian towns, Bag and Dány, where we organize after school activities for local children and youngsters. Volunteers will actively participate in the life of local communities, hold English-speaking group activities together with our experienced volunteers and plan team building workshops. Your tasks will include organizing and animating afternoon clubs, craft and sport days, helping in the organization and conduct of summer, spring and autumn camps, weekly visits in the local schools and many other thematically planned activities that focus on community development and disadvantage compensation.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Bagázs Közhasznú Egyesület in Budapest, Hungary; activity period 36 weeks within 1 September 2026 – 30 June 2027. Topics: anti-discrimination work, social inclusion and community work, civic participation, education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 32 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Our ESC volunteers will be accommodated in a shared apartment in Budapest close to the settlements where their activities are going to take place. They get monthly pocket money and food allowance. The travel costs to Hungary and back to their home country will be refunded based on the distance band limits imposed by the European Commission. Local transportation will be covered with monthly bus tickets. - The participants are going to be involved in the organization’s own trainings for the different activities and get support from the activity coordinator and mentors. - On-Arrival Training and Mid-Term Evaluation are held by the Hungarian National Agency. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Tallinna Laagna Kindergarten-School is a combined kindergarten and elementary school dedicated to supporting children with disabilities. Its aim is to provide education and help students develop essential social skills so they can lead independent lives in the future. The school creates opportunities for children's development by offering a safe, joyful, and comfortable environment, along with an individual approach tailored to each child’s needs. The target group consists of 36 school-aged children with special needs, ranging from 7 to 17 years old. Regular daily activities include lessons based on the national curriculum, as well as a variety of additional sessions led by teachers and therapists. After the obligatory classes, children enjoy a rest and lunch break, followed by optional leisure activities such as indoor and outdoor games. FOR MORE INFO & HOW TO APPLY:

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Tallinna Laagna Lasteaed-Põhikool in Tallinn, Estonia; activity period up to 9 months (1 October 2026 – 20 June 2027). Topics: social inclusion and community work, civic participation, health and wellbeing, education and non-formal learning, employment and entrepreneurship, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 38 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: ESC Volunteers will be provided with suitable accommodation conveniently located near their respective hosting organisation. Accommodation will typically be in a shared apartment or hostel, furnished with essential items. Rooms may be private or shared, depending on availability, with shared kitchen and bathroom facilities. Volunteers receive €5/day pocket money and additional €7/day food allowance, managing their own meals. International travel is reimbursed based on set travel budget and task related local transport is covered to full extent. Volunteers will take part in the ESC training cycle organized by the Estonian National Agency, which focuses on personal development and intercultural learning. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

The organisation coordinates the work of seven youth rooms based in different small towns. Local young people aged 7-26 are welcome to join wide range of leisure activities organised by the permanent staff. The volunteers will be assisting a team of youth workers in daily activities of the centers in various locations giving a chance to see many places including beautiful nature and meet people around Lääne-Harju county. The youth worker provide task related support and guidance to the volunteers. Developing ideas and taking initiative is encouraged and fostered. Lääne-Harju Youth and Cultural Center is open to host international volunteers who would become part of their community. FOR MORE INFORMATION & HOW TO APPLY:

about.en:
Social Welfare Home in Gdynia is a residential care home for elderly people who need daily support. Some residents may have difficulties with moving around, taking care of their health, or managing everyday tasks, so they are supported by professional staff. The home is located in a cosy and green area, close to a forest, and has its own garden. It is home to 79 residents who form a small community. For them, it is important not only to receive care, but also to have social contact, stay active, and feel included. The centre offers different activities that help residents maintain their physical and mental wellbeing. These include rehabilitation, therapeutic activities, Senior Club meetings, and various social and cultural events. As a volunteer, you will mainly support occupational therapy activities. This type of therapy helps residents stay active, develop their interests, and enjoy their time. You will also help organise holidays and special events.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Dom Pomocy Spolecznej w Gdyni in Gdynia, Poland; activity period up to 12 months (1 September 2026 – 31 August 2027). Topics: social inclusion and community work, health and wellbeing, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 29 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteer will be provided with: - accommodation in a rented flat, in 1-2 persons room shared with other volunteers - monthly pocket money and allowance - monthly budget for bus ticket in Gdynia. Volunteer is obliged to participate in two trainings provided by National Agency (On-arrival Training and Mid-term Training) as well as in the trainings organized and run by supporting organization. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

Auxilium is a social enterprise created in 1984 in Altamura; a Type A cooperative which manages social healthcare services. Auxilium operates in the sector of psychiatric, disability, the elderly, schooling, training and volunteering. The volunteer will take part in the implementation of various rehabilitation activities carried out in 2 different structure, to support educators and users. The volunteer will be initially trained about a correct approach with people with disabilities, working methods, spaces, roles and rules within it. Finally, the volunteer, assisted by an educator, will be involved in the daily life of the Centres, in its relations with users and the realization of activities. The volunteer has to take part in all the activities and to learn from every sector of the structure that is provided for the users. After the first months the volunteer will choose the activities he/she wants to develop more or/and develop a personal project inside the structure

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Auxilium in Altamura, Italy; activity period 24 weeks within 3 November 2026 – 1 May 2027. Topics: social inclusion and community work, health and wellbeing, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 28 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: The volunteers will be hosted in a shared flats in center of Altamura. The flat have a kitchen, living room, shared sleeping rooms, shared bathroom. The apartment is shared with other ESC volunteers, everyone is responsible for taking care for the flat - cleaning, shopping and cooking. Each month every volunteer has the right to receive a the pocket money and money for food. There is no need for transport because the working and living place are at walking distance. Read all details here: Long-term volunteers will be followed during all the activities by a tutor who will favor their job placement and integration within the working group, thus favoring one full and active participation in all the activities of the NGO. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
The Gdynia Social School is the primary school run by the association. The Social School is run by the association to introduce alternative methods of education. It focuses on working with kids also with special needs e.g. children with sight impairment, autism and other disorders or health problems. It is a small institution for 160 pupils 6-15 years old. We work in small groups of max 20 pupils. You will work in a group of 3 volunteers from different countries under the supervision of the school’s pedagogist. You will create integration and energizing games for kids, organize workshops, help teachers during the classes, work with kids with special needs, organize charity events, teach languages etc. All depend on your skills and interests!

about.en:
Located on the beautiful island of Saaremaa, Orissaare Youth Center offers the opportunity to support young people through youth work and non-formal learning while becoming part of a lively local community. The project focuses on creating meaningful opportunities for young people to develop their skills, confidence and creativity through workshops, cultural activities and everyday interactions. Volunteers contribute to a welcoming environment where young people are encouraged to participate and take initiative. At the same time, the project promotes intercultural learning by bringing together different cultures and perspectives, enriching both the local community and the volunteer's personal development. Through this experience, volunteers gain valuable insight into youth work, community engagement and life in a close-knit island community while making a positive impact on the lives of local young pe MORE INFO & HOW TO APPLY:

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Saaremaa Noorsootöö Keskus in Kuressaare, Estonia; activity period up to 8 months (25 October 2026 – 30 June 2027). Topics: social inclusion and community work, civic participation, environment and nature protection, health and wellbeing, education and non-formal learning, employment and entrepreneurship, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 37 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteers will be provided with suitable accommodation conveniently located near their respective hosting organisation. Accommodation will typically be in a shared apartment or hostel, furnished with essential items. Rooms may be private or shared, depending on availability, with shared kitchen and bathroom facilities. Volunteers receive €5/day pocket money and additional €7/day food allowance, managing their own meals. International travel is reimbursed based on set travel budget and task related local transport is covered to full extent. Volunteers will take part in the ESC training cycle organized by the Estonian National Agency, which focuses on personal development and intercultural learning. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
The aim of this ESC project (11 months) is to introduce young people to the reality of out-of-school education institution and its activities, help them improve their skills and abilities, foreign language while at the same time allowing them to learn new ones. For some this can also be the first time they are out of their home, in a foreign country and on their own. We are here to help them with all of those things. Volunteer's role will mostly consist of cooperation with people in our organisation and social media. Volunteers will help them with ongoing activities prepared by the Centre for leisure time activities. They will be working with children and youth in the culture area like dance, music, but they can also be active in areas corresponding to their hobbies and interests that are available, like chess, floorball, falconry or languages to name a few. In addition, we organize big events for our town like International Children's day, St. Nicolaus Day and also summer camps.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Centrum volneho casu in Stará Ľubovňa, Slovakia; activity period 48 weeks within 1 October 2026 – 30 September 2027. Topics: education and non-formal learning, culture and creativity, sport and physical activity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 38 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Rented flat, shared with up to 3 volunteers. Each volunteer gets their own room, with kitchen and bathroom being shared. Travel costs for the arrival/departure are covered. Transport in town is not needed, since the flat is less than 10 minute walk from the organization. However, public transport is available, as is the local train and bus station. The volunteers are able to use their kitchen to cook food or they can join us for regular lunch at one of the restaurants (or some common lunches / celebrations). Pre-departure training will be the task of your Sending organization. On arrival training roughly weeks to about 2 months after their arrival, to be conducted by our National Agency (place and time chosen by the NA, changes all the time) with other volunteers staying in the country. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
Avec le soutien de l’équipe d'animateurs nature, vous aurez un rôle actif dans la vie quotidienne de Moulin Nature. Ils participeront à l’animation sociale et à la conception des programmes pour les familles et les seniors (ateliers au jardin, rencontres thématiques). Vous serez co-créateurs de nouveaux outils pédagogiques ludiques, tels que des escape games nature ou des jeux de plateau, pour sensibiliser les publics de manière innovante. Votre mission inclura également l'animation du jardin pédagogique, pour en faire un espace vivant et accueillant, ainsi que la création d'une signalétique écologique facilitant l'appropriation du site par tous. Pendant les vacances, vous serez impliqués dans la mise en place des séjours écoresponsables pour les ados (séjours itinérants en canoë et séjours européens).

about.en:
La mission proposée par l’association Sahel Vert vise à promouvoir une écologie politique à travers des activités concrètes telles que le maraîchage, le recyclage, la gestion forestière et l’intervention en milieu scolaire. Le volontaire intègre une équipe pluridisciplinaire et, après trois semaines d’observation, propose un projet-action personnel valorisant ses compétences et celles du collectif. Il bénéficie d’un accompagnement hebdomadaire et de formations adaptées. L’expérience permet de développer des compétences collaboratives, linguistiques et méthodologiques, tout en sensibilisant aux enjeux sociaux et éducatifs. Les volontaires, souvent confrontés à des réalités similaires à celles des publics accueillis, contribuent à lutter contre la stigmatisation et à impulser des dynamiques de développement local.
