about.en:
Volunteers will support several local community projects focused on sustainability, social inclusion and practical help for residents. At the second-hand shop and recycling project, volunteers help with sorting, cleaning, repairing and presenting donated goods. They support the shop, assist with customer contact and contribute to reuse, recycling and upcycling activities. At Het Dagelijks Bestaan (HDB), volunteers help with growing vegetables, preparing soup and meals, baking bread and delivering food to local residents. Through this work, they also offer social contact and help reduce loneliness in the neighbourhood. At Buurtservice Perspectief, volunteers support practical tasks for residents, such as garden maintenance, small household jobs, cleaning up public spaces and helping with local neighbourhood initiatives. All activities are carried out under supervision. These tasks give volunteers practical work experience, social skills and a better understanding of local community.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Stichting Flex fleks in Zutphen, Netherlands; activity period 60 weeks within 10 October 2026 – 30 November 2027. Topics: social inclusion and community work, environment and nature protection, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 25 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: Volunteers will be accommodated in shared housing in Zutphen. Each volunteer will have their private room and will share facilities such as the kitchen, bathroom and living areas with other volunteers. Food support will be provided through a weekly food allowance. Volunteers will also receive weekly pocket money, paid according to the European Solidarity Corps rules and agreed arrangements. During the ESC project, volunteers must attend the mandatory On-Arrival and Mid-Term Trainings. The dates are fixed and cannot be changed. These trainings support learning, personal development and reflection during the project. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
As part of this project, volunteers will be actively involved in organising and delivering non-formal educational activities for children and young people in placement centres, primary schools, and kindergartens located in disadvantaged areas of Reșița. Through workshops, games, creative activities, and intercultural learning experiences, volunteers will support participants in developing essential life skills, building self-confidence, enhancing creativity, and discovering new interests. The project aims to encourage active participation, inclusion, tolerance, and mutual respect while creating a positive environment where children and young people feel supported and motivated to learn and grow. During the summer, volunteers will also coordinate and work alongside short-term volunteers, helping to plan activities, facilitate teamwork, and ensure a meaningful learning experience for everyone involved.

about.en:
KC Kláštor is a vibrant cultural and community center in the heart of Rožňava, a town in eastern Slovakia known for its historical architecture, proximity to the Slovak Karst, and a peaceful yet open community atmosphere. As a volunteer, you will support the center's team in organizing cultural events, workshops, and community activities for people of all ages. You will be part of a team that runs the accommodation, café, kitchen, and of course, cultural programming, aiming to contribute to the development of the local community. We warmly welcome your own ideas, skills, and cultural perspectives. The center prides itself on an open and inclusive environment where every idea and every person has a place. This is a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience in community development and cultural management, build confidence in working with people, and experience everyday life in a small yet lively Slovak town close to nature.

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Otvor Dvor in Rožňava, Slovakia; activity period up to 12 months (1 September 2026 – 1 September 2027). Topics: civic participation, health and wellbeing, employment and entrepreneurship, culture and creativity. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 43 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: We will provide volunteers with suitable accommodation located directly on the host organization's premises, featuring a private room with a shared kitchen and bathroom. Volunteers receive pocket money of €5 per day and a food allowance of €7 per day, and are responsible for preparing their own meals. International travel costs are reimbursed within the set budget, and local transport related to your duties is fully covered. Volunteers will take part in the ESC training cycle organized by the Slovak National Agency, which focuses on personal development and intercultural learning. As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

about.en:
We welcome volunteer artists from EU countries, aged 18-30, in fields such as music, dance, painting, photography, pottery, weaving and traditional crafts. Our organization promotes these crafts in Roma communities and works with young people and adolescents. The volunteer program offers an opportunity to interact with a different culture - one where music and dance are the most captivating forms of entertainment, interaction and joy. Our goal is to build an intercultural bridge between Roma and non-Roma youth. We hope that this project will serve as a model of fruitful cooperation, inclusion and community responsibility. We invite you to join us for a unique volunteering experience! Vous ne serez de pas de simples observateurs, mais des acteurs impliqués dans la création d’un environnement convivial et solidaire. Votre mission consistera à favoriser les échanges entre les participants, encourager la mixité sociale et culturelle, et contribuer à la sensibilisation à une alimentation durable. Concrètement: Vous participerez à l’animation sociale en accueillant les convives, en facilitant les interactions et en créant une atmosphère chaleureuse. Vous animerez des ateliers interculturels, par exemple en organisant des repas thématiques, afin de valoriser la diversité culturelle et de stimuler la curiosité des participants. Vous participerez aussi à vulgariser ce concept auprès des jeunes. Plus d'infos :  | Vidéo de présentation :

about.en:
Individual volunteering: Are you eager to help us out with our daily activities at a unique off-grid location, where you can develop practical skills in animal care, renovation, and green maintenance? Are you someone who likes animals and nature, while trying something out of your comfort zone? This is a project for those who love practical outdoor work, aren't afraid to get their hands dirty, and have a go-getter mentality with a proactive attitude. We place a strong emphasis on sustainable living. Our animal family includes 2 cows, 3 ponies, sheep, 2 pigs, chickens, geese, an aviary, 2 dogs, and a cat. The tasks are physically demanding, and the weather can be challenging in the Netherlands during November and December. We are looking for around 3 individuals!

Practical details: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering hosted by Stichting BioArt Laboratories in Eindhoven, Netherlands; activity period 64 days (9 November 2026 – 11 January 2027). Topics: environment and nature protection. Residents of Georgia are explicitly accepted, together with 17 other countries. Applications are rolling, so apply early.

Living and learning: The accommodation is at BioArt Village, a beautiful location surrounded by a forest inside the city of Eindhoven. The place is off-grid, fulfilling basic needs, and participants must approach this with a non-wasteful mindset. Common areas include the bathroom, kitchen, and living room. In addition to pocket money, you also receive food money, so basic cooking skills are necessary. The center and shops are around 25 minutes by bike. Airport is nearby. Our project offers multiple durations, so there is something for everyone. We provide short-term volunteering with a minimum duration of two months, and long-term volunteering when possible (up to 6 months). As in every ESC project, accommodation, food, local transport, insurance and pocket money are covered, travel is reimbursed by distance band, and volunteers get training, a mentor, language support and a Youthpass certificate.

en: Individual European Solidarity Corps volunteering in Eindhoven, Netherlands
Focus: environment and nature protection
Rolling applications; residents of Georgia eligible

eligibility.en: Young people aged 18–30 (you can register from 17) resident in one of the 18 accepted countries listed on the European Youth Portal, which include Georgia: Azerbaijan, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czechia, France, Georgia, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Luxembourg, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden. Host's profile: We are looking for volunteers who are interested in nature, like physical outdoor work, and who embrace living off-grid. They should be ready to tackle challenges, capable of daily sustainable animal care, outdoor work, and assisting with restoring the area. Participants are able to work independently and effectively as team players. A positive attitude and strong motivation are essential. The place is quiet and serene with nature, so the project resonates more with those who have an affinity with nature, quietness and respect for animals.

en: Check you are 18–30 and live in one of the accepted countries listed on the opportunity page.
Register on the European Solidarity Corps section of the European Youth Portal and complete your profile.
Open the opportunity page and click Apply, attaching your CV and a motivation statement.
Contact a supporting (sending) organisation in your country; in Georgia, Youth Association DRONI acts as an ESC sending organisation.
Prepare for an online interview with the host before selection.

costs.en: Free for the volunteer. The European Solidarity Corps covers accommodation, food or a food allowance, local transport, insurance and monthly pocket money, and reimburses international travel by distance band.

score_reason: Fully funded ESC placement that explicitly accepts residents of Georgia; verified open on the European Youth Portal

about.en:
Ladder to Inclusion is a free self-paced online course run by the Hungarian youth NGO Élményakadémia (Academy of Experience) with Associazione JOINT, Asociación Las Niñas del Tul and MARTA Centres. It helps youth workers and organisations make international youth mobility (youth exchanges, volunteering, ESC and other non-formal learning projects) safer, more inclusive and empowering for highly vulnerable young people.

The course covers safeguarding, risk management, trauma-informed and solution-focused approaches, preparing and supporting participants before, during and after a mobility, professional boundaries, crisis response and self-care, using practical examples and reflection exercises. It is aimed at youth workers, trainers, youth leaders, project managers, volunteering mentors, coaches and teachers; up to 500 participants, in English.

It is listed on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar for Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU (including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova and Ukraine) and other countries. There is no fee, and you can start any time after registering.

about.en:
Youth+ is a free self-paced online course by Academy of Experience (Élményakadémia) with Outward Bound Romania, Via KreAction and Marta Centre. It teaches youth workers, teachers and facilitators how to support groups of young people with fewer opportunities to create and carry out their own volunteering projects, and is also useful for anyone mentoring ESC volunteers or groups.

The course is built on the field-tested "From Us to You" programme, used since 2011 with Hungarian young people in foster care and segregated minority communities, and gives an overview of experiential education, solution-focused and trauma-informed approaches. Up to 500 participants; working language English; a Youthpass certificate is available. The course is still in beta and asks for feedback through built-in forms.

It is listed on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar for Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU (Georgia included) and other countries. No fee; start any time after registering.
